title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Grothendieck's 'Longue Marche' / 'équation des lacets' setting. pi_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, a free group F_2. Autext_lac(pi^_{0,3}) is the group of outer automorphisms of its profinite completion that respect the 'lacets', i.e. that send inertia generators to conjugates of their powers. This is the ambient group of what became GT^.

Previous page. The homomorphism Psi' : N'_{1,1} -> GL(2,Z^)/Z^*_2 factors the earlier Psi. Grothendieck asks how to lift it to (34) N'_{1,1} -> GL(2,Z^)/{±1}. The original N_{1,1} -> GL(2,Z^) would then follow by pulling back along 1 -> ±1 -> GL(2) -> GL(2)/±1 -> 1. Here N_{1,1} is the extension of the arithmetic group by pi_1 of the modular stack M_{1,1}.

This page.
1. He declares the essential question to be determining the lift (34) of (32).
2. He restarts the argument abstractly. Take any subgroup Gamma of Autext_lac(pi^_{0,3}) commuting with the outer action of S_3; Gal(Qbar/Q) and GT^ are examples. This gives an extension M_{0,3} (= N'_{1,1}) of Gamma by S^+_{0,3}. Equivalently it is an extension of S_3 x Gamma by pi^_{0,3}.
3. S^+_{0,3} is the profinite completion of the extension 1 -> F_2 -> PSL(2,Z) -> S_3 -> 1, coming from Gamma(2)/±1 = F_2 and PSL(2,F_2) = S_3. So S^+_{0,3} = PSL(2,Z)^, written SL(2,Z)'^ with ' meaning mod ±1. Geometrically it is the orbifold pi_1 of M_{0,4}/S_3 = M_{1,1} mod the elliptic involution.
4. (36): conjugation inside M_{0,3} gives a homomorphism M_{0,3} -> Aut(PSL(2,Z)^) that restricts to inner automorphisms on S^+_{0,3}.
5. (37): there is an injection GL(1,Z^) -> Aut(PSL(2,Z^)), given by conjugation by diag(lambda,1).
6. Gamma is restricted (the S_3-commutation already forces this) by a congruence condition. The congruence completion map (38) PSL(2,Z)^ -> PSL(2,Z^) must be Gamma-equivariant (next page). On the source Gamma acts by outer action via transport of structure. On the target it acts via the cyclotomic character chi : Gamma -> Z^* composed with Z^* -> Z^*/Z^*^2 = image in Out.
7. Next page: this congruence condition yields phi' : M_{0,3} -> GL(1,Z^). Pairing it with chi, the 'congruence conditions' force a factorization psi' : M_{0,3} -> GL(2,Z^)/_2Z^*.

The goal is to reconstruct the Galois (or GT-type) representation on Tate modules of elliptic curves, i.e. the map to GL(2,Z^), purely from the action on pi^_{0,3}. This requires the action to descend through the congruence kernel ker(PSL(2,Z)^ -> PSL(2,Z^)).
errors: Phrasing gap: (37) is injective into Aut, but in Out only Z^*/Z^*^2 survives. Conjugation by diag(mu,mu^-1), which lies in SL, equals conjugation by diag(mu^2,1). The next page correctly uses Z^*/Z^*^2 for outer actions; this page leaves the Aut/Out distinction implicit.

Gap: it is not justified that the congruence-compatibility condition is 'déjà conséquence' of S_3-commutation. For general Gamma commuting with S_3 (e.g. GT^-type groups) it is unclear that the congruence kernel of PSL(2,Z)^ is Gamma-stable. The text oscillates between calling it a consequence and imposing it as a condition (next page: 'Cette condition de congruence définit...').

ideas.what: Identification of the S_3-extension of pi^_{0,3} with the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) (Gamma(2)/±1 = F_2, quotient S_3)
ideas.modern_name: pi_1^orb(M_{1,1}) / elliptic involution = PSL(2,Z)^; Lambda(2) level structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; used in GT context by Ihara, Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, M_{1,1})

ideas.what: Abstract framework: arbitrary subgroup Gamma of lacet-preserving outer automorphisms commuting with S_3 gives an extension M_{0,3}, and a homomorphism to Aut(PSL(2,Z)^)
ideas.modern_name: action of GT^ (or subgroups) on PSL(2,Z)^ / B_3^ mod center

ideas.what: Congruence condition: require Gamma-equivariance of the congruence quotient PSL(2,Z)^ -> PSL(2,Z^), with action on the target via the cyclotomic character mod squares; used to reconstruct a GL(2,Z^)-valued (Tate-module) representation
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of GT^-action with the congruence kernel; 'congruence' subgroup of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: for Galois: classical (Tate module of Legendre/Tate curve); for GT^: partially Nakamura, Lochak-Schneps, Boggi, Hoshi-Minamide-Mochizuki-type work (unsure)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes defining a GT-like subgroup of Autext_lac(pi^_{0,3}) by a 'congruence condition': its action on PSL(2,Z)^ must preserve the congruence kernel and induce the cyclotomic action on PSL(2,Z^). From such a group he aims to construct canonically a homomorphism to GL(2,Z^)/±1, the analogue of the Galois action on elliptic-curve Tate modules. Whether GT^ itself satisfies this, i.e. preserves the congruence kernel, and the explicit lift (34), are left open.
missed.quote: la question essentielle semble ici la détermination du relèvement (34) de (32)... la condition que l'extension (38) Ŝ^+_{0,3} → SL(2,Ẑ)' [soit] compatible aux actions ext. de Γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether GT^ is compatible with congruence quotients of PSL(2,Z)^ (equivalently, whether a GT^-representation on 'Tate modules' exists) bears on whether GT^ = G_Q and on modular-tower versions of GT. Imposing this as a defining condition gives a possibly smaller GT-variant that does not seem to be standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Using compatibility with the congruence quotient of PSL(2,Z)^ as a defining condition on a GT-type group is a natural but not standard refinement. The aim of extracting a GL(2,Z^) 'Tate module' representation from a purely combinatorial lacet-preserving group is interesting. Much of the setup, though, is known in later GT literature.
transcription_corrections: In (38) the subscript under Ŝ^+_{0,3} reads 'SL(2,Z)'^' (profinite completion of SL(2,Z)'), with ∪/'≅' sign, and the target is SL(2,Ẑ)'.
Struck text before (38) reads roughly 'ext. → ext.^ → S', a cancelled attempt.
The crossed passage reads roughly 'Utilisons et l'iso Ŝ^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Ẑ)', ... thomomorphismes'; it is replaced by 'd'où un homomorphisme'.
'restreint (c'est une déjà conséquence...' — 'déjà' is an interlinear insertion.
